text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- The government is about to privatise its 82 percent stake in the Cahora Bassa hydroelectric dam in Mozambique, worth 450 billion escudos. Negotiations are taking place with South Africa which has a monopoly of the distribution of Cahora Bassa's energy.
- The management of state airline TAP has signed an agreement with ground staff for a salary rise of 3.5 percent.
- BP/Mobil is studying the possibility of lowering its petrol prices to maintain its competitiveness against Esso which has cut prices by three escudos per litre in some places.

- The commissioner of Lisbon's Expo '98 world fair, Torres Campos, said in an interview that any losses incurred by the exhibition will come out of the state budget over a long period of time to reduce the immediate impact on tax payers.
- Portugal and Spain have secured a guarantee that European Union aid to olive oil producers will not be changed.

- French retail group Auchan intends to open seven new hypermarkets in Portugal, representing an investment of 20 billion escudos, the chairman of the group for the Iberian Peninsula, Francis Lepoutre, said.

- The government is preparing for the streamlining and possible privatisation of cereal distributor EPAC. A document will be sent to Brussels for a decision by the European Commission which is expected in October.
